entrypoints.claim_limit: Tested local continuity primitive; no exact external chat handover or universal effect enforcement proof.

Opt-in supervisor composes the existing acknowledged gateway, hosted client and optional Companion for a new ARE-owned session. The development-only cross-OS WSL parent launches that managed session and exposes loopback observation without becoming a second reasoning controller. Normal Windows turn ingress remains paused because the hook callback boundary is unverified. An explicit guarded text-only development mode has fixed-loopback and extracted-package evidence, including a fresh parent/listener heartbeat in the read-only Companion view, but no live-provider, installed-package, wider effect-coverage, or existing-desktop-task handover proof. Neither supervisor activates this desktop task.

Wraps one Codex process without the acknowledged gateway recovery contract. Its current shared wrapper assesses three approval requests, passes three explicit client interaction/read requests, and denies other or unknown host server requests before client delivery; this does not make direct mode an activated session controller.

Opt-in, version-bound WSL desktop command adapter. Explicit direct-candidate mode starts the direct stdio wrapper; managed-gateway mode starts the separate acknowledged desktop client and has no direct fallback. It pins the backend and admits only observed launch forms. Standalone managed protocol canaries passed, but isolated desktop launches did not invoke the shim. It does not transfer an existing task or prove desktop UI ingress, exclusive writer, complete effect coverage, or rollback. The discontinued TUI is not a fallback.

Opt-in WSL JSONL client for the acknowledged ARE gateway with private request and delivery state. Installed-backend protocol canaries cover initialize and bounded elicitation without a desktop-owned UI task. It is not an existing-task handover, complete native protocol proof, or activated desktop controller.

Independently runnable, version-bound stdio proxy with its own approval and continuation handling; it does not use the persistent gateway or its acknowledged recovery. Its effect binder recognizes session-wide and policy-amending acceptances, so it does not inherit the newer wrapper's one-use approval guard. Historical digest-bound bindings remain unchanged.
Environment-configured Workspace desktop bridge starts a separate ephemeral Codex thread through the legacy proxy; it is not an acknowledged gateway client or an activated existing desktop task.

Legacy unacknowledged stdio client now reuses the validated gateway receipt and JSON-lines transport; it still has no durable resume-secret recovery or activation eligibility for an existing desktop task.
Programmatic acknowledged gateway client used by an isolated native-hook canary; hook observations remain advisory and do not establish installed desktop-task control.

Interactive local browser client over the gateway. Normal Windows turn ingress remains paused; the explicit guarded text-only candidate permits only the restricted new-session path. A content-free latest accepted-turn receipt, isolated browser recovery canary and guarded fixed-loopback turns do not prove live-provider compatibility, wider effect coverage, same-desktop-task handover, or resolution of truly unknown backend delivery.

Explicit local JSON-lines interaction harness owns a file-backed wrapper and injected response provider, not a gateway consumer or desktop-host session. It is backend development evidence, not a replacement product UI or an activated chat controller.

Define conversation client defaults to the acknowledged gateway on its own fixed codex:define-cli consumer, separate from the hosted codex:human-chat client; a second simultaneous Define attachment is rejected. It can explicitly use the direct Codex stdio wrapper, whose continuity differs. Its implementation binding is candidate-stale, and neither consumer ID is an exact host-task identity.

Executable coding-agent demo starts one ephemeral Codex thread through the direct stdio wrapper and can apply a bounded fixture patch only with explicit approval. It does not use acknowledged gateway continuity, own this desktop task, or establish a product chat controller.

Configured proposal, iterative session, and approved candidate-apply executable owns its own bounded coding-agent state and model transport. Optional recommend-only Evolution remains separate; this is not a host chat session or desktop-task writer.

Disposable scripted-model fixture demonstrates one bounded coding-agent candidate and optional explicit approval in a temporary tree. It is neither live model ingress nor a product conversation interface.
Customer launcher runs the direct Codex stdio wrapper with a checked customer profile and writer lock; it is not an acknowledged persistent-gateway client or this desktop task's writer.

Website-local, no-tool conversation controller imports ARE conversation, routing and context modules but owns separate process-memory sessions and a distinct lightweight Reasoning State format; it is not the persistent gateway.
Closed public HTTP reverse proxy for the website; it does not select routes, own conversations, or dispatch model turns.
Website model-call quota and accounting boundary; it owns neither the chat session nor provider credentials.
Website's fixed provider request and dedicated credential/egress boundary; not an ARE conversation gateway or interchangeable with a general model transport.

Discontinued TUI interface retained as source provenance only. Its in-process Conversation Runtime client has no production gateway, backend-thread identity or external-host handover binding; it is not a current product UI target.

Discontinued TUI coding-proposal interface retained as source provenance only, not a current product UI target. Its acknowledged gateway consumer and private resume/turn-intent records do not restore a lost proposal, release an uncertain turn, or bind the current desktop task.
Bounded no-tool pilot composes the existing gateway, hook callback and a local provider proxy; it is not a second product controller or a live desktop-task integration.
Disposable scripted coding-agent artifact fixture with no live model, host chat or persistent gateway ownership.
Default backend adapter; exact installed host capability and task identity must be verified.
One-shot text-only DSH bridge; durable backend history is opt-in through the gateway CLI with an existing DSH home, and gateway recovery is a distinct state layer.
Process transport shape only; no host-protocol or lifecycle conformance is implied.
Orchestrator command-to-AgentTurn adapter has a transport trait and deployment socket configuration, but no admitted live ARE socket transport; it is not a chat-session writer.
Caller-carried, non-executing decisions; not a chat transport.
Local tool interface reusing non-executing decisions and separately gated, potentially state-changing Evolution commands; not a chat turn writer or read-only observer.
Advisory host observations; callback bridge is used by the native canary, not installed as an enforcing gateway.

Opt-in exact-session C1 projection from a verified checkpointed ledger; an isolated selected-PATH-CLI canary delivered it before the next model request, but not through the current desktop task, an installed hook, or automatic mid-turn compaction.
Internal conversation identity is not bound to a gateway consumer or external host thread in the production entrypoint.
Single model-turn/provider adapters, not host conversation controllers.
Separate one-request accounting and token-bound transport; overlaps HTTP wiring but cannot replace the general provider facade without preserving its stronger proof contract.
Bounded retrieval inside coding-agent context; no host session ingress or authority.
Explicit semantic, source and route-availability capability adapters; no chat transport, route invention or effect authority.
Read-only doctor and opt-in development-only gateway adapter, thread and decision projections; these are in-process observations, not packaged live activation status or exact host-task ownership.
Improvement and worker coordination boundaries; neither owns chat ingress.
Optional product declaration points to development integration evidence, not an installed desktop bridge.
Required product ontology/package validation integration, not a chat client or gateway.

overlap_groups.decision: One exclusive acknowledged writer is the activation target; retain current alternatives as compatibility or experimental paths without equivalent-control claims.

Bind and reconcile current gateway consumer, backend thread, website session, local interaction ledger, Define conversation and ARE conversation identities; do not merge their different stores by name alone.
These are distinct controller modes with different durability and effect capabilities; select one per bound conversation and prove migration before any consolidation.
Separate configured candidate execution, direct-host demonstration, scripted fixtures, exchange fixtures and Orchestrator command adapters; none supplies an existing-chat writer by itself.
Reuse one decision implementation but keep non-executing, tool, and advisory enforcement postures distinct.

The current wrapper and hosted client decline session-wide or policy-amending acceptance; the legacy proxy still has distinct acceptance semantics and hooks remain advisory. None of these proves universal interception of host effects.
Share only transport primitives whose timeout, credential and response contracts match; preserve recycling-specific token and one-request proofs.
Record separately bound current Workspace, website, customer, Define, pilot, exchange and Orchestrator paths; neither names nor imported modules establish shared controller ownership.
Preserve discontinued TUI source and evidence as history only; neither client participates in current turn ingress, identity reconciliation, or product UI work.
Retain separate HTTP ingress, quota and credential-egress boundaries; share only proven protocol primitives, not their authorities or failure policies.

open_questions: Can the installed desktop task hand over its exact history to an exclusive ARE gateway writer?
Which backend capability evidence and recovery proof are sufficient for each selected interaction client?
Which owner approves retirement of compatibility entrypoints after migration evidence?
How will the website's process-memory Reasoning State and inferred-route no-match behavior align with the selected ARE conversation contract without fabricating route authority?
